The mark had come only from the census readers' lists of what they could not read, so every counted page was screened for a sign of a barrier (the page's own structured data saying it is not free to read, a subscribe or sign-in phrase in the text or the HTML, a paywall marker with a short text, or a text under 2,000 characters; scripts/as_built/nv8_partial_screen.py) and the 248 pages the screen listed were read one by one by a reader from another model family, with 15 pages of known state mixed in as controls (research/nv8_pages_in_part_read.tsv): the reader judged 210 whole, 37 part and could not tell for 1; the controls came back as known except three posts of one aggregator-style site, judged part because they quote part of another outlet's report. Those posts, and three more like them among the pages read, are kept as whole (the post is the piece that was listed, and its text is all here), with the reader's verdict and this reason in the table. 92 counted pages are now marked as held in part (58 before). The figure's sentence gives both numbers and says what was not read again: a page of more than 2,000 characters that shows no sign of a barrier.
